    Forbidden configurations #

    Proof of Proposition 4.1, Step 2: "A vertex of degree at least four would contain a four-leaf star, and the vector z with entries two at the centre and one at the leaves satisfies zᵀMz = 0 on it. Two trivalent vertices would contain their connecting path and two extra edges at each end; weights two on the path and one on its four leaves again give a nonzero vector z with zᵀMz = 0. Both contradict positive definiteness of principal submatrices."

    With the configuration bound (qform_le_config), the extra edges of the whole graph only lower zᵀMz, so each configuration gives zᵀMz ≤ 0.

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.arm_sum_aux (L : ℕ) :
    2 * ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (L + 1), (↑j + 1) ^ 2 - 2 * ∑ j ∈ Finset.range L, (↑j + 1) * (↑j + 2) = (↑L + 1) * (↑L + 2)

    The sum identity behind the arm computation.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.arm_contribution (L : ℕ) :
    ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (L + 1), 2 * ((↑L + 1 - ↑k) / (↑L + 2)) ^ 2 - 2 * ((↑L + 1) / (↑L + 2)) - ∑ k ∈ Finset.range L, 2 * ((↑L + 1 - ↑k) / (↑L + 2) * ((↑L - ↑k) / (↑L + 2))) = -((↑L + 1) / (↑L + 2))

    The arm computation (the Schur complement at the centre): for one arm of length L + 1 with weights (L + 1 - k)/(L + 2), its contribution is -(L+1)/(L+2).

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.arm_inequality {D : Type v} [Fintype D] [DecidableEq D] (G : SimpleGraph D) [DecidableRel G.Adj] {n : D → ℚ} (hn : ∀ (i : D), 0 < n i) (hMn : ∀ (i : D), 0 < 2 * n i - ∑ j ∈ G.neighborFinset i, n j) {t : ℕ} (L : Fin t → ℕ) (c : D) (a : (i : Fin t) → Fin (L i + 1) → D) (hinj : Function.Injective (Sum.elim (fun (x : Unit) => c) fun (x : (i : Fin t) × Fin (L i + 1)) => a x.fst x.snd)) (hc : ∀ (i : Fin t), G.Adj c (a i 0)) (ha : ∀ (i : Fin t) (k : Fin (L i)), G.Adj (a i k.castSucc) (a i k.succ)) :
    ∑ i : Fin t, (↑(L i) + 1) / (↑(L i) + 2) < 2

    The arm inequality (Schur complement at the centre): a centre with t arms of lengths L_i + 1 satisfies ∑_i (L_i + 1)/(L_i + 2) < 2, i.e. 2 - ∑ p_i/(p_i + 1) > 0 for arm lengths p_i.
